data.other_hard: first time applicants to Sciences Po; household does not file taxes within the European Union (tax residence of parents, not the student; financial independence needed for country of residence to count); not Swiss or Norwegian applicants; not candidates with dual citizenship including an EU citizenship; not Quebec candidates for master's degree; not master's dual-degree candidates unless in listed programmes; not PhD, 1-year master, bachelor dual-degree (unless agreement), exchange, or French graduate admission procedure candidates; cannot be combined with other Sciences Po or partner scholarships; not possible while on deferral
data.evidence_sentence: To be eligible for the scholarship, students must be: first time applicants to Sciences Po, from a non-European Union state, whose household does not file taxes within the European Union, and who have been admitted to the Undergraduate or Master's programme.
data.notes: Page covers both undergraduate and master's programmes; amounts differ (bachelor total exemption or EUR 9,500 fee exemption; master EUR 18,500 per year for two years). Master's deadlines are listed without a year, so annual dates used. Undergraduate deadlines are for 2027 entry. Selection is on merit and tied to admissions; no minimum grade stated. Renewal is automatic for master's continuation at Sciences Po, and applicants must be admitted to apply. Applicants from French secondary schools use Parcoursup and a separate form. Page lists Swiss, Norwegian and other exclusions in detail; the nationality rule is approximated as non-EU state group.
